jp: 私[わたし]は後輩[こうはい]に数学[すうがく]を教[おし]え{てあげました|gv-teageru}。
en: I taught maths to my junior as a favour.
why: I am the one doing the favour for someone else, which is てあげる; the others make me the receiver.

jp: クラスメートが風邪[かぜ]で休[やす]んだので、授業[じゅぎょう]のノートを見[み]せ{てあげました|gv-teageru}。
en: My classmate was away with a cold, so I showed them my class notes.
why: I did the favour for my classmate, so てあげる; てくれる or てもらう would mean the classmate helped me.

jp: 留学生[りゅうがくせい]の宿題[しゅくだい]を、放課後[ほうかご]に手伝[てつだ]っ{てあげました|gv-teageru}。
en: I helped the exchange student with their homework after school.
why: The speaker does a kindness for the student, so the giving form てあげる is used.

jp: 同僚[どうりょう]が遅[おそ]くまで残業[ざんぎょう]していたので、お弁当[べんとう]を買[か]っ{てあげました|gv-teageru}。
en: My colleague was working late, so I bought them a boxed meal.
why: I did something for a colleague, which is てあげる; the other forms would make me the one who benefits.

jp: 友達[ともだち]の作文[さくぶん]の間違[まちが]いを直[なお]し{てあげました|gv-teageru}。
en: I corrected the mistakes in my friend's essay for them.
why: I am the helper and the friend benefits, so てあげる is right.

jp: 新入社員[しんにゅうしゃいん]にコピー機[き]の使[つか]い方[かた]を教[おし]え{てあげるつもりです|gv-teageru}。
en: I intend to show the new employee how to use the copier.
d: てくださるつもりです
why: The speaker plans to do the favour for the newcomer, so てあげる; the others describe someone helping me.

jp: 試験[しけん]の前[まえ]に、友達[ともだち]に勉強[べんきょう]のコツを教[おし]え{てあげたいです|gv-teageru}。
en: Before the exam I would like to teach my friend some study tips.
why: The wish is to do the favour for the friend, so てあげたい; てもらいたい would mean wanting the friend to teach me.

jp: 隣[となり]の席[せき]の子[こ]に消[け]しゴムを貸[か]し{てあげました|gv-teageru}。
en: I lent an eraser to the child sitting next to me.
why: I lent it to the other child, so てあげる; the others would mean the child lent it to me.

jp: 会議[かいぎ]の準備[じゅんび]が間[ま]に合[あ]わない同僚[どうりょう]を、私[わたし]が手伝[てつだ]っ{てあげました|gv-teageru}。
en: I helped a colleague who could not finish preparing for the meeting in time.
why: 私が is the helper and the colleague is helped, so てあげる.

jp: 入学式[にゅうがくしき]の後[あと]、新入生[しんにゅうせい]に学校[がっこう]の中[なか]を案内[あんない]し{てあげました|gv-teageru}。
en: After the entrance ceremony, I showed the new students around the school.
why: I guided the new students for their benefit, so てあげる; the others would mean the new students showed me around.

jp: 部活[ぶかつ]の後輩[こうはい]の発表[はっぴょう]の練習[れんしゅう]に付[つ]き合[あ]っ{てあげました|gv-teageru}。
en: I stayed with my club junior and practised their presentation with them.
why: I did my junior the favour, so てあげる is right.
